turns.message: Route optimization targets road freight, which is 41.7% of total logistics cost, with fuel taking 42.1% of road cost. Larger fleets already have GPS and dispatch systems, keeping operational risk low. While empty-run reduction addresses reported 40% empty runs, route optimization offers the most immediate path forward with existing fleet technology.

Our messy data directly threatens demand forecasting, which explicitly needs clean order history. Empty-run reduction depends on an unverified 40% figure and requires fragmented fleets to share data. Furthermore, SME consolidation struggles because SMEs have thin data and little digital infrastructure, and warehouse manpower estimates of 30% remain unverified.

adjustments.reason: Forecasting requires clean order history, which is compromised by messy and scattered data.
Reported 40% empty runs figure is unverified and requires fragmented fleets to share data.

verdict.summary: Messy internal data and unverified benchmarks severely limit advanced forecasting and multi-party coordination initiatives. Route optimization remains the only viable immediate investment because road freight dominates logistics spend and larger fleets already possess GPS infrastructure.
